proof_nl:
Fix n>1 and an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1. Let x,y be real numbers such that m/n<=x<=y<(m+1)/n. Then m<=nx<=ny<m+1, so floor(nx)=floor(ny)=m. Also, for each k=1,2,...,n, since x<=y and k>0 we have kx<=ky, hence floor(kx)<=floor(ky). Therefore
F_n(x)-F_n(y) = (floor(nx)-floor(ny)) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)-floor(ky))/k
= sum_{k=1}^n (floor(ky)-floor(kx))/k >= 0,
because each summand is nonnegative and each k is positive. Thus F_n(x)>=F_n(y), so F_n is nonincreasing on [m/n,(m+1)/n).
solver_summary: On the interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), the term floor(nx) is constant, while each floor(kx) is nondecreasing in x; hence the whole expression cannot increase.
vetter_reason: The argument correctly shows that for x,y in the same interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), both floor(nx) and floor(ny) equal m, and each floor(kx) is at most floor(ky) since x<=y and k>0. Hence F_n(x)-F_n(y) is a sum of nonnegative terms, proving F_n is nonincreasing on each such interval.
